C-ADD-AMBIENT-MUSIC.IntentSummary: Add a looping ambient music channel beside the interface sounds, with its own service, preference, life-cycle pause and fades, and move the audio control from the hub into the shared header as one icon opening a two-switch menu.

MustPassCommand.Command: grep -q 'class SoundService' lib/services/sound_service.dart && grep -q 'class SfxPlayer' lib/services/sfx_player.dart
grep -q 'assets/music/' pubspec.yaml && test "$(ls assets/music/*.mp3 | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" -eq 2

T-001.Title: Lay out the two music tracks and record their provenance

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: assets/music/ holds almost-floating.mp3 and deep-space-loop.mp3, checked with the system tooling as valid stereo MP3 at 48 kHz and about 3-4 minutes each.
assets/music/SOURCES.md names Open Lo-Fi, the CC0-1.0 license, the release URL, and both titles with their durations.
pubspec registers assets/music/ alongside the existing asset folders.

Verification.Command: for f in assets/music/*.mp3; do afinfo "$f" | grep -E 'estimated duration|Data format'; done

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: lib/services/music_player.dart declares a MusicPlayer interface that can start a looping track, set the volume, stop, and report when a track finishes.
The audioplayers implementation sets ReleaseMode.loop for a single track and exposes completion so the service can advance; failures degrade to silence instead of throwing.
Nothing else in the app learns about the engine: audioplayers is imported by exactly the two adapter files.

T-003.Title: Add the music service: preference, rotation, fades and life cycle

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: MusicService extends ChangeNotifier with enabled, volume, load, setEnabled and dispose, persisting to the ui_music_enabled key.
It rotates: when a track finishes, the next one starts, wrapping around.
It observes the app life cycle, pausing when the state is not resumed and returning only if music is enabled.
Volume eases in and out rather than jumping, and the track never plays when music is off or in tests.
The default is on at 0.25, and the observer is removed in dispose.

T-004.Title: Register the music service in the app scope

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: AppScope provides MusicService and calls its load, next to the interface sound service, with a comment only if the order is not obvious.

T-005.Title: Move the audio control into the shared header as a two-switch menu

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: AdaptiveNavBar carries one control, placed with the existing header actions near the clock, that opens a menu with a switch for interface sounds and a switch for ambient music, each reading and writing its own service.
The control's icon reflects whether either channel is on, so a glance says whether the app is muted.
The layout survives both the desktop top bar and the phone bottom bar: tabs, the central button and the clock keep their places.
lib/pages/home_page.dart loses its own switch and the hub's Services row returns to a plain title.

T-006.Title: Prove the music service's four behaviours with a fake player

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: test/music_service_test.dart injects a fake player and asserts that a disabled service never starts a track, that enabling starts it, that disabling stops it, and that finishing a track advances to the next one.
The test touches no platform channel and needs no device.

T-007.Title: Extend the durable audio module and its verification

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: M-SOUND's summary in the graph describes the audio layer as two channels — interface sounds and ambient music — rather than sounds alone.
V-M-SOUND gains the music command and scenarios, including that silence when music is switched off is a valid outcome and that playback stops when the app leaves the foreground.
